Gene Munster Sees Strong Demand for Apple’s Duo iPhone
On Friday, Munster said on
X
that the Duo was "off to a solid start," predicting the device could lift Wall Street’s fiscal 2027 iPhone growth forecast from 10% to 13%.
In a blog post, Munster said his observations during the first hour of the launch revealed surprisingly long lines, despite the device’s high price.
"My initial read on the first hour of the Duo launch is that lines are surprisingly long given the high price point," he wrote.
Munster raised his confidence in his forecast of 20 million Duo sales in fiscal year 2027, equivalent to about 7% of total iPhone units, compared with Wall Street’s estimate of roughly 12 million.
How Apple’s Duo Could Add $8 Billion In Revenue
The additional 8 million units could contribute approximately $8 billion to Wall Street’s $279 billion iPhone revenue estimate for fiscal year 2027, Munster said.
His calculations assume customers switch from phones with an average selling price of $1,200 to the Duo, which carries an estimated $2,200 average selling price.
Munster expects the Duo to account for 8% of iPhone unit sales and 16% of revenue in fiscal year 2027, compared with Wall Street’s projections of 4% and 7%, respectively.
Why Shorter Launch Lines Don’t Worry Munster
Munster noted that Duo launch-day queues were roughly half as long as those observed during the 2018
iPhone XS
and
XS Max
launches.
However, he attributed the difference partly to higher prices and the shift toward online orders and carrier-assisted upgrades.
He also pointed to iPhone growth accelerating from 0% in fiscal year 2024 to 4% in fiscal year 2025, with 21% expected in fiscal year 2026, despite shorter launch-day lines.
"The bottom line is Apple has discovered a new lever in the iPhone growth equation that should help boost overall revenue growth by 3% in FY27 and 5% in FY28," he stated.
Adding, "The Street is currently looking for 10% iPhone growth in FY27 and 8% in FY28. So I believe the Duo will slightly bump up those growth rates."
The Duo is off to a solid start and should take the Street’s FY27 iPhone growth from 10% to 13%.
